annotations.text:
CHOSEN — ALPENGLOW

Night granite (#0E1012), one alpenglow accent (#FF6B3D) used only for sport marks, podium placings and hover. Bebas Neue set huge over Barlow, IBM Plex Mono for every number.

Race results are a dense eight-column table — everything visible at a glance, which is what a tracker wants.

Nav stays the same four items sitewide — Notes / Speaking / Athlete / Contact — so there is never a dead end. Only the skin changes at /athlete.

Races, times and placings are invented samples. The Strava panel is sample data until the API app exists.

PHOTOS

Dashed boxes mark the slots. This direction leans hardest on the hero.

• 1 hero — 2400×1200 landscape
• 3 action shots — 1200×900, one each for skimo, trail, climbing
• optional per-race thumbnails — 400×300

Until they arrive the hero is a drawn ridge silhouette, which holds up on its own.

STRAVA

The "This week" panel is sample data. Real activities need a Strava API application and a server-side refresh-token exchange — access tokens expire every six hours, so a static token won't hold.

Built as one swappable block so nothing else changes when it gets wired.

NOT CHOSEN

B — Contour: warm sandstone, pine and rust, contour lines behind the mastheads, race ledger with per-row elevation sparklines.

C — Summit Log: the existing paper/ink system one degree warmer with a single rust accent, reusing the /speaking row shape.

Kept for reference — the sparkline idea from B and the year-grouped list from C are both easy to graft onto Alpenglow later.
